goal: `mc gate <files…>` runs named test files with the `node --test` flags the repository declares (`pr_tests_flags`), so a memoro test that imports `/js/…` runs in a session as it runs in memoro's own runner.

`mc shot dev --compare <ref>` does not wait a quarter of an hour for a slot that mc's own superseded compare server holds: an idle superseded compare server is stopped, the ref side waits at most 60 s, and a refusal names the compare servers already running.
A dev server registered for a worktree whose process runs in another directory is never reused for that worktree, and `mc dev list` says so.
`mc shot` takes `--click <selector>`, repeatable, and never presents a picture taken without the clicks as one taken with them.
contract: The dev-server protocol is unchanged: no manifest field is added or required, and `mc dev list --json` prints exactly what it prints today (memoro's wrapper runs it before every register).
The capture request gains one field, `click`, after `onboarding`; every other request field and every result field mc already reads keeps its meaning.
Admission (`admission`, `admit`, the two-server cap, the memory floor) is unchanged. Only the wait `--compare` asks for on its ref side is shorter.
mc stops no dev server except a compare server under `~/.memoro/mc/compare/` for the same worktree name, idle for more than 15 minutes, stopped through its own stop command.
Every existing `mc gate`, `mc shot`, `mc dev` and `mc test dev` behaviour not named in a step stays as it is.
out_of_scope: Reusing seeded data across `--compare` runs (proposal item 2). It is a later decision. Step 2 adds only the help sentence that `--compare <sha>` pins the tree and its database.

memoro's side of `--click`: `scripts/shot/request.mjs` accepting `click` and `scripts/shot/shot.mjs` clicking each entry and answering `clicked`. It is in `~/mc/proposals/2026-10-18-memoro-shot-click-and-fresh-bundle.md`.
memoro's measure server and `scripts/dev.mjs` clearing or rebuilding `public/dist/` and `public/modules/` on start, and a `built_from.bundle` manifest field. In the same memoro proposal.
The stale `public/dist/app.html`, `module-manifest.json` and `public/modules/` from 2026-09-15 in `~/memoro`: the planning session removed them on 2026-10-18.
A cwd check anywhere but `ensureDevServer` and the text of `mc dev list`: `servingWorktree`, `serversFor`, the page and `mc test dev --list` read the registry as before.
Changing which worktree `mc shot` or `mc test dev` chooses (`shotWorktree`, `sharedWorktree`, `--here`).

steps.title: `mc gate <files…>` runs named files with the declared pr_tests_flags
steps.done_when: `src/mc/gate-fast.js` exports `primaryCheckoutDeclaration` and `declaredTestFlags`, `primaryDeclaration` uses the first, `src/mc/commands/gate.js` passes `declaredTestFlags(io, { root, env })` to `namedCommand` for named files; the new tests in `tests/mc/gate-command.test.js` and `tests/mc/gate-fast.test.js` pass; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: on 2026-10-17 a memoro step session ran `mc gate tests/…` on a test that imports `/js/msr/runtime/card-derivation-registry.js` and got `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. memoro's own runner (`scripts/testing/runner.mjs`) runs `node --test --import ./tests/_helpers/browser-paths.mjs`, which rewrites `/js/…` imports. mc already knows this: the shipped gate table declares `pr_tests_flags: ['--import', './tests/_helpers/browser-paths.mjs']` for memoro (`src/mc/repo-gate-table.js` line 250) and `['--import', './tests/_isolate-home.mjs']` for memoro-cli (line 152). `namedCommand` (`src/mc/gate-local.js` lines 66–71) takes a `flags` option that replaces the flags read off the `test` script, and a test covers that option (`tests/mc/gate-local.test.js` line 214). But `src/mc/commands/gate.js` line 121 calls `namedCommand(manifest, files, { pattern })` without `flags`, so for memoro, whose `test` script is `node scripts/testing/ci.mjs`, `testFlags` finds no flags and node runs bare. The incremental path already reads the declaration (`primaryDeclaration`, `src/mc/gate-fast.js` lines 185–199); the named-files path never did. `git log -S pr_tests_flags -- src/mc/commands/gate.js` on origin/main is empty.

In `src/mc/gate-fast.js`, split `primaryDeclaration` (line 185). Add above it, exported, with a one-line doc comment ('The primary checkout of the worktree at `root` and its gate declaration, or null when either cannot be read.'): `export function primaryCheckoutDeclaration(io, { root, env }) { const common = io.git(root, ['rev-parse', '--path-format=absolute', '--git-common-dir']); if (!common) return null; const primary = dirname(common); let declared = null; try { declared = io.declaration(primary, { env }); } catch { return null; } return declared?.ok && declared.declaration ? { primary, declaration: declared.declaration } : null; }`. Then, exported, with the doc comment 'The `node --test` flags the primary checkout declares (`pr_tests_flags`), or null when it declares none — then the `test` script's own flags stand.': `export function declaredTestFlags(io, { root, env }) { const flags = primaryCheckoutDeclaration(io, { root, env })?.declaration?.pr_tests_flags; return Array.isArray(flags) && flags.length ? [...flags] : null; }`. Rewrite `primaryDeclaration` to start with `const found = primaryCheckoutDeclaration(io, { root, env }); if (!found) return null; const select = found.declaration.select; if (!select) return null;`, use `found.primary` where it used `primary` for `selectionStateDir`, and `found.declaration.pr_tests_flags` for `flags`. Its result `{ select, env, flags }` is unchanged, so `incrementalPlan` does not change.

In `src/mc/commands/gate.js`, add `declaredTestFlags` to the import from `'../gate-fast.js'` (line 49). Change line 121 to `const command = files.length ? namedCommand(manifest, files, { pattern, flags: declaredTestFlags(io, { root, env }) }) : gateCommand(manifest, { base });`. In the header comment (lines 10–15) and in `usage()` (line 313), the named-files form now reads: 'the named test files, with the node --test flags the repository declares (pr_tests_flags), else those of its test script'. Keep the usage line's other words.

Tests in `tests/mc/gate-command.test.js`, inside `describe('mc gate <test files…>')` (line 140), using `harness()`. The existing tests stay green unchanged: the harness `git` answers `null` for `--git-common-dir` (its `args[1]` is `--path-format=absolute`), so `primaryCheckoutDeclaration` returns null and the `test` script's flags stand. (1) 'named files run with the declared pr_tests_flags, which replace the test script\'s': `const { out, deps } = harness({ manifest: { scripts: { test: 'node scripts/testing/ci.mjs' } }, tests: ['tests/x.test.js'], finishAfter: 1, output: 'ℹ tests 1\nℹ fail 0\n' }); const plain = deps.git; deps.git = (cwd, args) => (args.includes('--git-common-dir') ? '/repo/x/.git' : plain(cwd, args)); const asked = []; deps.declaration = (path) => { asked.push(path); return { ok: true, declaration: { pr_tests_flags: ['--import', './tests/_helpers/browser-paths.mjs'] } }; };` then `assert.equal(await run(['tests/x.test.js'], deps), 0)`, `assert.equal(out.spawned[0].args[1], `node --test --import ./tests/_helpers/browser-paths.mjs tests/x.test.js; echo $? > '${EXIT}'`)` and `assert.deepEqual(asked, ['/repo/x'])`. (2) 'a declaration without pr_tests_flags leaves the test script\'s flags': the same, with `manifest: { scripts: { test: TEST_SCRIPT } }`, `tests: ['a.test.js']` and `deps.declaration = () => ({ ok: true, declaration: { select: 'node select.js' } })`; the spawned command is `node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs a.test.js; echo $? > '${EXIT}'`.

Test in `tests/mc/gate-fast.test.js`, a new `describe('declaredTestFlags')` at the end of the file, importing `declaredTestFlags` from `'../../src/mc/gate-fast.js'` beside what the file already imports. One `it('declaredTestFlags reads the primary checkout\'s declaration')` with a hand-made io: `const io = (answer) => ({ git: (cwd, args) => (args.includes('--git-common-dir') ? '/repo/x/.git' : null), declaration: answer });`. Assert: `declaredTestFlags(io(() => ({ ok: true, declaration: { pr_tests_flags: ['--import', './a.mjs'] } })), { root: '/w/x', env: {} })` deepEquals `['--import', './a.mjs']`; `io(() => ({ ok: true, declaration: {} }))` gives null; `io(() => ({ ok: true, declaration: { pr_tests_flags: [] } }))` gives null; `io(() => ({ ok: false, reason: 'x' }))` gives null; `io(() => { throw new Error('bad file'); })` gives null; and an io whose `git` returns null for everything gives null. Every existing test in the file passes unchanged.

Docs: in `docs/mc-command-matrix.md`, the row `mc gate [--test-name-pattern

]` (line 64) begins 'The named files with this repository's node --test flags (the `--import`s and `--experimental-*`s of its `test` script)'. Make it: 'The named files with the node --test flags the repository declares (`pr_tests_flags` in the gate table or its `.mc/test.json`, read from the primary checkout as the incremental gate reads it), else the `--import`s and `--experimental-*`s of its `test` script'. Put this edit in a last commit that touches nothing else. Add `changelog.d/gate-files-declared-flags.md` with `section: Fixed` and one entry: '**`mc gate ` runs named files with the declared `pr_tests_flags`.** It read flags only off the `test` script, and memoro's is `node scripts/testing/ci.mjs`, so a memoro test importing `/js/…` failed with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND where memoro's runner adds `--import ./tests/_helpers/browser-paths.mjs`. The flags come from the same declaration the incremental gate already read.'

steps.title: `--compare` stops a superseded idle compare server and waits at most 60 s for a slot
steps.done_when: `src/mc/shot-compare.js` exports `COMPARE_ADMIT_WAIT_SECONDS`, `COMPARE_IDLE_MS`, `stopSuperseded` and `runningCompares`, and `runCompare` stops superseded idle compare servers, asks admission for at most 60 s and prints the running-compare line on a `cap` refusal; `ensureDevServer` and `ensureAppServer` carry `refused`; `mc shot` usage has the `--compare <sha>` sentence; the new tests in `tests/mc/shot-compare.test.js` and `tests/mc/test-environment.test.js` pass; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: on 2026-10-17 a memoro step session ran `mc shot dev … --compare origin/main` and watched 'mc: waiting for a slot — held by …' for minutes with no way out. The compare tree is keyed by commit: `compareTree` (`src/mc/shot-compare.js` line 41) uses `~/.memoro/mc/compare/<basename(worktree)>-<sha10>`. Once `origin/main` moves, the new sha gets a new directory, and that needs a new server. The previous compare tree's server is still live, and `admission` (`src/mc/dev-servers.js` lines 291–311) exempts only the asker's own worktree and service, so the old compare server counts as one of the two holders (`DEFAULT_MAX_SERVERS = 2`, line 271). The wait is not endless: `ensureDevServer` asks `admit` with `waitSeconds: deps.admitWaitSeconds ?? 900` (`src/mc/test-environment.js` line 374), polls every 10 s and says so once a minute (`ensureAppServer`, line 454). But it is a quarter of an hour, spent mostly waiting on mc's own leftover. Measured 2026-10-18: `~/.memoro/mc/compare/` held four trees (`memoro-6a4cb31e83`, `memoro-7b58e77292`, `memoro-9962a0f341`, `memoro-ce2e824888`). Every workarea's memoro checkout is named `memoro`, so the name prefix alone also matches other sessions' compare trees. That is why only an idle one is stopped: `compareTree` touches the directory on every reuse (lines 43–46), so its mtime is its last use.

In `src/mc/test-environment.js`, `ensureDevServer` line 381 becomes `if (!admitted.ok) return { ok: false, error: refusalText(admitted), refused: admitted };`, and `ensureAppServer` line 456 becomes `if (!ensured.ok) return { ok: false, error: ensured.error, ...(ensured.refused ? { refused: ensured.refused } : {}) };`. Nothing else in either function changes.

In `src/mc/shot-compare.js`: add `import { serversUnder, stopServer } from './dev-servers.js';` and `import { log } from './logger.js';`. Below `DAY_MS` add `/** How long the ref side of a compare waits for a slot: a minute, not the quarter of an hour a plain start waits. */ export const COMPARE_ADMIT_WAIT_SECONDS = 60;` and `/** A compare tree unused this long is not in the middle of a capture, and its server may be stopped to free a slot. */ export const COMPARE_IDLE_MS = 15 * 60 * 1000;`. Add a private helper `compareRootOf(deps)` returning `deps.compareRoot || join(mcHome(deps.env || process.env), 'compare')`, and `siblings(worktree, keep, deps)`: `const root = resolve(compareRootOf(deps)); const prefix = `${basename(worktree)}-`; return (deps.serversUnder || serversUnder)(root).filter((server) => server.live !== false && server.resource_class !== 'light' && server.worktree_path && dirname(resolve(server.worktree_path)) === root && basename(server.worktree_path).startsWith(prefix) && resolve(server.worktree_path) !== resolve(keep)).map((server) => ({ server, sha: basename(server.worktree_path).slice(prefix.length) }));`.

Add, exported, with a doc comment saying what the Why paragraph says in two sentences: `export function stopSuperseded(worktree, keep, deps = {})`, returning `{ stopped: [ids], lines: [strings] }`. First: if `(deps.serversFor || serversFor)(keep).some((server) => server.resource_class !== 'light')`, return `{ stopped: [], lines: [] }`, because the asked tree is already served and needs no slot. Then for each `{ server, sha }` of `siblings(worktree, keep, deps)`: read `mtimeMs` of `server.worktree_path` with `(deps.statSync || statSync)` in a try (skip on error); `idle = (deps.now ? deps.now().getTime() : Date.now()) - mtimeMs`; skip when `idle <= COMPARE_IDLE_MS`. Stop through `(deps.stopServer || stopServer)(server)` in a try/catch (an exception is `{ ok: false, error: message }`). Log `log('dev-server-stopped', { instance_id: server.instance_id, service: server.service ?? null, worktree_path: server.worktree_path, reason: 'compare-superseded', ok })`. On success push the id and the line `stopped ${server.instance_id}, the compare server of ${sha} idle ${Math.round(idle / 60_000)} min, to free its slot`; on failure push only the line `could not stop ${server.instance_id}, the compare server of ${sha}: ${error}`.

Add, exported: `export function runningCompares(worktree, keep, deps = {})` returning the line, or null when `siblings(worktree, keep, deps)` is empty: `running compare servers: ${list.map(({ server, sha }) => `${sha} (${server.url})`).join(', ')} — --compare ${list[0].sha} reuses one, with its tree and its database`.

In `src/mc/commands/shot.js` `usage()`, directly after the `[--compare <ref>]` line (line 398), add the line `'                                      --compare <sha> pins the tree and its database\n',`. In `docs/technical/mc-shot.md`, at the end of the `--compare <ref>` bullet (lines 87–97), add: 'A compare tree is per commit, so `--compare origin/main` after main moved needs a new tree and a new server. The compare server of an older commit of the same worktree name, unused for 15 minutes, is stopped first to free its slot (`mc: stopped <id>, the compare server of <sha> idle <n> min, to free its slot`). The ref side waits at most 60 s for a slot. A refusal names the compare servers still running, and `--compare <sha>` reuses one of them, with its tree and its database.' In `docs/mc-command-matrix.md`, append to the `mc shot` row (line 71), after '…and the measured numbers that moved.': ' An idle compare server of an older commit is stopped to free its slot; the ref side waits at most 60 s, and `--compare <sha>` pins the tree and its database.' Put both docs edits in a last commit that touches nothing else.

Tests in `tests/mc/shot-compare.test.js`. Add `stopSuperseded`, `runningCompares` and `COMPARE_IDLE_MS` to the import from `'../../src/mc/shot-compare.js'`. A new `describe('a superseded compare server')`, before `describe('mc shot dev --compare')`: make `home = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'mc-shot-supersede-'))`, `root = join(home, 'compare')`, and directories `memoro-1111111111`, `memoro-2222222222`, `memoro-3333333333` (the kept one), `memoro-5555555555` and `other-4444444444` under it. Use `const NOW = new Date(2026, 9, 18, 12, 0, 0);`. With `utimesSync`, set `memoro-1111111111`, `other-4444444444` and `memoro-5555555555` to 20 minutes before `NOW`, and `memoro-2222222222` to 5 minutes before. `const servers = ['1111111111', '2222222222', '5555555555'].map((sha) => ({ instance_id: `srv-${sha}`, service: 'memoro-measure', worktree_path: join(root, `memoro-${sha}`), url: `http://127.0.0.1:89${sha[0]}0`, resource_class: sha === '5555555555' ? 'light' : 'standard', live: true })).concat([{ instance_id: 'srv-other', service: 'memoro-measure', worktree_path: join(root, 'other-4444444444'), url: 'http://127.0.0.1:8944', resource_class: 'standard', live: true }]);`. (1) 'stops only an idle compare server of the same worktree name, through its own stop': `const stops = []; const freed = stopSuperseded(join(home, 'memoro'), join(root, 'memoro-3333333333'), { compareRoot: root, now: () => NOW, serversUnder: () => servers, serversFor: () => [], stopServer: (server) => { stops.push(server.instance_id); return { ok: true }; } });` then `stops` deepEquals `['srv-1111111111']`, `freed.stopped` the same, and `freed.lines` deepEquals `['stopped srv-1111111111, the compare server of 1111111111 idle 20 min, to free its slot']`. (2) 'stops nothing when the asked tree is already served': the same call with `serversFor: () => [{ live: true, resource_class: 'standard' }]` and a `stopServer` that throws; `freed.stopped` deepEquals `[]`. (3) 'a stop that fails is said, not counted': `stopServer: () => ({ ok: false, error: 'no stop command' })` gives `stopped` `[]` and `lines` `['could not stop srv-1111111111, the compare server of 1111111111: no stop command']`. (4) 'runningCompares names every running compare server of the name, idle or not': `runningCompares(join(home, 'memoro'), join(root, 'memoro-3333333333'), { compareRoot: root, serversUnder: () => servers })` equals `'running compare servers: 1111111111 (http://127.0.0.1:8910), 2222222222 (http://127.0.0.1:8920) — --compare 1111111111 reuses one, with its tree and its database'`, and with `serversUnder: () => []` it is null. `rmSync(home, { recursive: true, force: true })` in a `finally`.

In the same file, extend `compare()` (around line 212): it takes `{ measures = {}, warnings = {}, refuse = null, running = [] } = {}` and returns `waits` too. Its deps gain `compareRoot: join(home, 'compare')`, `serversFor: () => []`, `stopServer: () => ({ ok: true })` and `serversUnder: () => running.map((sha) => ({ instance_id: `srv-${sha}`, service: 'memoro-measure', worktree_path: join(home, 'compare', `memoro-${sha}`), url: 'http://127.0.0.1:8930', resource_class: 'standard', live: true }))`. Its `ensureAppServer` stub becomes `async (dir, declaration, opts) => { servers.push(dir); waits.push(opts?.deps?.admitWaitSeconds); if (refuse && dir !== worktree) return { ok: false, error: refuse.error, refused: refuse.verdict }; … as before }`, with `const waits = [];`. The existing four tests pass unchanged; the directories in `running` do not exist, so `stopSuperseded` skips them on `statSync`. New test in `describe('mc shot dev --compare')`: 'a refused ref server waits at most 60 s and names the running compare servers': `const result = await compare(['dev', 'assistant', '--compare', 'origin/main'], { running: ['6a4cb31e83'], refuse: { error: '2 of 2 app servers already running — srv-a (/x), srv-b (/y); stop one with mc test dev --stop in its worktree', verdict: { ok: false, reason: 'cap', holders: [] } } });` then `result.code` is 1, `result.waits` deepEquals `[undefined, 60]`, `result.stderr` matches `/mc: origin\/main: 2 of 2 app servers already running/u` and includes the line `mc: running compare servers: 6a4cb31e83 (http://127.0.0.1:8930) — --compare 6a4cb31e83 reuses one, with its tree and its database`, and `result.stdout` is ''. The same with `verdict: { ok: false, reason: 'memory', holders: [], free_percent: 9 }` and `error: 'only 9% memory free (floor 15%)'` prints no `running compare servers` line.

Test in `tests/mc/test-environment.test.js`, in `describe('admission before a start')`, the test 'does not spawn when admission refuses' (line 1024): after its existing assertions add `assert.equal(ensured.refused.reason, 'cap');` and `assert.equal(ensured.refused.holders.length, 2);`.

Add `changelog.d/compare-slot.md` with `section: Fixed`: '**`mc shot dev --compare` stops its own superseded compare server instead of waiting for it.** A compare tree is per commit, so after main moved the previous compare server held one of the two slots and the ref side waited up to 15 minutes. Now a compare server of an older commit of the same worktree name, unused for 15 minutes, is stopped through its own stop command; the ref side waits at most 60 s; and a refusal names the running compare servers, any of which `--compare <sha>` reuses with its tree and its database.'
`mc gate tests/mc/shot-compare.test.js tests/mc/test-environment.test.js tests/mc/shot.test.js`, then `mc gate`, `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`.

steps.title: A dev server whose process runs outside its registered worktree is refused and flagged
steps.done_when: `src/mc/dev-servers.js` exports `processCwd` and `strayCwd`; `ensureDevServer` refuses a registered server whose process cwd is known and is not the worktree, without stopping it or starting another; `mc dev list` text marks such a server and `--json` is unchanged; the new tests in `tests/mc/dev-servers.test.js` and `tests/mc/test-environment.test.js` pass; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: on 2026-10-08, in the ui-faults workarea, `mc test dev --list` named `http://127.0.0.1:8920` as the server for `/Users/martinforsberg/mc/ui-faults/memoro`. But `lsof -p` showed its `measure-server.mjs` and `workerd` processes running with cwd `/Users/martinforsberg/memoro`. The page loaded `/modules/chunks/canvas.a6d9034b.js`, a bundle from 2026-09-15 that still had a hover card deleted on 2026-10-01. So a screenshot that was supposed to show the worktree showed another tree's old frontend. mc chooses by registration alone: `servingWorktree` (`src/mc/test-environment.js` lines 146–151) matches `worktree_path`, and `ensureDevServer` (line 318) reuses that server after checking git (`builtFromMoved`, `editedSince`) and health. Nothing compares the process with the worktree. `servedTree` (`src/mc/commands/shot.js` lines 308–320) prints the worktree's own branch and commit, so 'serving <worktree>' repeats the registration's claim. Measured 2026-10-18 with `mc dev list` and `lsof -a -p <pid> -d cwd -Fn`: all three registered servers (8920 in `~/mc/step/msr-core-residue/memoro`, 8911 and 8910 in two plan checkouts) run in their own worktree, so the mismatch does not show today. memoro's measure server derives its root from its own script path and spawns with that cwd (`scripts/testing/measure-server.mjs` lines 100, 236, 733), so how the 2026-10-08 mismatch arose is unknown. The check makes it impossible to miss either way. The stale bundle itself is memoro's: the worker prefers `public/dist/app.html` when it exists, and that file is a gitignored build leftover. Clearing it is out of scope here.

In `src/mc/dev-servers.js`, add `realpathSync` to the `node:fs` import (line 36). After `serversUnder` (line 443), add, exported: `/** The working directory of a running process, as lsof reads it, or null when it cannot be read. */ export function processCwd(pid, { run = spawnSync } = {}) { try { const asked = run('lsof', ['-a', '-p', String(pid), '-d', 'cwd', '-Fn'], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 5000 }); if (asked?.status !== 0) return null; const line = String(asked.stdout || '').split('\n').find((item) => item.startsWith('n')); return line ? line.slice(1) : null; } catch { return null; } }`. Then `/** A registered server whose process runs somewhere other than its worktree: { cwd }, or null when it runs there or when that cannot be read — unknown is trusted, as a manifest without built_from is. */ export function strayCwd(server, { cwdOf = processCwd } = {}) { if (!server?.pid || !server.worktree_path) return null; const cwd = cwdOf(server.pid); if (!cwd) return null; return real(cwd) === real(server.worktree_path) ? null : { cwd }; }` and a private `function real(path) { try { return realpathSync(path); } catch { return resolve(path); } }`. realpath matters: on macOS `lsof` reports `/private/var/…` for a path under `/var/…`.

In `src/mc/test-environment.js`, add `processCwd` and `strayCwd` to the import from `'./dev-servers.js'` (lines 33–35). In `ensureDevServer`, directly after `const running = servingWorktree(worktree, { root, service });` (line 327), add: `const stray = running ? strayCwd(running, { cwdOf: deps.processCwd || processCwd }) : null; if (stray) { log('dev-server-stray', { instance_id: running.instance_id, service: running.service ?? null, worktree_path: running.worktree_path ?? null, server_pid: running.pid ?? null, cwd: stray.cwd }); return { ok: false, error: `${running.instance_id} is registered for ${worktree} but its process runs in ${stray.cwd} — not reused; mc dev stop ${running.instance_id}, then run this again` }; }`. Add one sentence to the doc comment above `ensureDevServer`: 'A registration whose process runs in another directory (`strayCwd`) is refused, never reused and never stopped: it is somebody's server, and only a person knows whose.' Do not stop it and do not start another, since its port and its registration would collide.

In `src/mc/commands/dev.js`, add `processCwd` and `strayCwd` to the import from `'../dev-servers.js'` (line 61). In `run`, line 90 becomes `if (opts.verb === 'list') return list(opts, { stdout, root, cwdOf: deps.processCwd || processCwd });`. In `list` (line 107), take `cwdOf`. In the text loop only (line 118), compute `const stray = strayCwd(server, { cwdOf });` and append `stray ? `  (runs in ${stray.cwd} — not this worktree's)` : ''` to the line. The `--json` branch is untouched and never calls `cwdOf`, because memoro's wrapper runs `mc dev list --json` before every register.

In `docs/dev-server-protocol.md`, at the end of '## Who reads the inventory' (after line 50), add: 'A registration is still a claim. Since 2026-10-18 `ensureDevServer` also reads the registered process's working directory (`lsof -d cwd`) and refuses a server whose process runs outside the worktree it is registered for, without stopping it: on 2026-10-08 a server registered for a workarea ran in the shared checkout and served its three-week-old frontend. `mc dev list` marks such a server `(runs in <cwd> — not this worktree's)`; `--json` is unchanged. A cwd that cannot be read is trusted.' Put it in a last commit that touches nothing else.

A new `describe('a server that runs somewhere else')`: (1) 'processCwd reads lsof's n line, and null on any failure': `processCwd(123, { run: () => ({ status: 0, stdout: 'p123
fcwd
n/Users/x/memoro

steps.title: `mc shot --click <selector>`, repeatable, refused when the capture script does not say it clicked
steps.done_when: `scanArgs` takes `repeatable`, `mc shot` reads `--click` with it, `buildRequest` sends `click` after `onboarding`, `clickGap` in `src/mc/shot.js` is checked after every capture in `src/mc/commands/shot.js` and on both sides in `src/mc/shot-compare.js`; the new tests in `tests/mc/commands/flags.test.js`, `tests/mc/shot.test.js` and `tests/mc/shot-compare.test.js` pass; every `success_criteria[].met` in this plan is true; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: on 2026-10-17 a memoro step session needed before and after shots of the week focus on a phone. The task rows sit behind the 'Tasks' tab, and the entity's action window needs a person opened and the tasks count pressed. `mc shot` could not press anything. Only a target declared in memoro's `.mc/shot.json` can click, through `open: [{ click }]`, which memoro's `scripts/shot/shot.mjs` runs in `openWindow` as `page.locator(step.click).first().click({ timeout: 10_000 })`. Declaring a target is a memoro change outside a step, so the session wrote its own Playwright script. mc has no browser: it hands the capture script one request file (`buildRequest`, `src/mc/shot.js` lines 244–268) and reads one result line. So `--click` is a request field, and memoro's script has to perform it. That memoro part is not in this plan. Until it lands, memoro's `validateRequest` (`scripts/shot/request.mjs`) ignores a field it does not know, and today's script would take the picture without clicking. So mc asks for proof: a capture asked to click must answer `clicked`, a list as long as the request's `click`, or mc exits 1 and says the picture was taken without the clicks. This step lands before memoro supports it, and until memoro does, that refusal is the honest answer to every `--click`.

In `src/mc/commands/flags.js`, `scanArgs` takes a fourth kind, `repeatable = []`: strict value flags that may be given more than once, collected in order into an array. Initialise `for (const name of repeatable) flags[key(name)] = [];`. Add `if (repeatable.includes(arg)) { strictPending = arg; continue; }` beside the `strictValues` check (line 44). Where a strict value is stored (line 38), push when the pending flag is repeatable: `if (repeatable.includes(strictPending)) flags[key(strictPending)].push(arg); else flags[key(strictPending)] = arg;`. Missing values are refused exactly as for `strictValues` ('--click needs a value'). Add one paragraph to the header comment: '`repeatable` is `strictValues` for a flag given more than once (`mc shot --click`): each value, in order, in an array that is empty when the flag is not given.'

In `src/mc/shot.js`, `buildRequest` takes `click = null` and appends `click: Array.isArray(click) && click.length ? [...click] : null,` after `onboarding`. Add, exported, after `parseResult`: `/** A capture asked to click and answered by a script that does not say it clicked as many: the picture is of the page without the clicks. The sentence, or null when nothing was asked or every click was answered. */ export function clickGap(request, result) { const asked = Array.isArray(request?.click) ? request.click : []; if (!asked.length) return null; if (Array.isArray(result?.clicked) && result.clicked.length === asked.length) return null; return `the picture at ${result?.file} was taken without the clicks — this memoro's capture script does not answer clicked, so --click is not supported yet (memoro's scripts/shot/shot.mjs has to honour request.click)`; }`.

In `src/mc/commands/shot.js`: the `scanArgs` call (line 52) gains `repeatable: ['--click']`. `buildRequest({ … })` (line 183) gains `click: flags.click`. Import `clickGap` from `'../shot.js'` (lines 34–37). After the `typeof result.file` check (lines 229–232), add `const gap = clickGap(request, result); if (gap) { stderr.write(`mc: ${scrub(gap)}
`); return 1; }`. Nothing goes to stdout, so `$(mc shot … | head -1)` gets no path for a picture that is not the one asked for. In the header comment's synopsis (lines 4–9), add `[--click <selector>]…` after `[--measure <css> | @<name>]`. In `usage()`, after the `--measure` lines (line 393), add `'          [--click <selector>]        press it after the page and its window are open and before
',` and `'                                      --wait-for/--scroll/--el; repeatable, in order; a CSS selector
',` and `'                                      or text=<words>, as memoro's capture script reads locators
',`.

In `src/mc/shot-compare.js`, import `clickGap` beside `runCapture` from `'./shot.js'` (line 18). In `runCompare`'s capture loop, after the `typeof result.file` check (lines 165–168), add `const gap = clickGap(req, result); if (gap) { stderr.write(`mc: ${label}: ${scrub(gap)}\n`); return 1; }`. The ref request is a copy of `request` (line 153), so it carries the same `click`.

Docs: in `docs/technical/mc-shot.md`, add a bullet at the end of the list under '## Measuring a layout (2026-10-15)' (after the `--compare` bullet, line 97): '**`--click <selector>`** (repeatable): pressed in order after the page and its target's window are open, before `--wait-for`, `--scroll` and the subject, so a pane behind a tab or a window behind a button can be pictured without declaring a target. A CSS selector, or `text=<words>`, as memoro's capture script hands it to Playwright. The request carries `click: [..]` (null without the flag), and the result must answer `clicked`, a list as long as the request's. A result without it is a capture script that ignored the field, and mc exits 1 with `the picture at <file> was taken without the clicks — …` and prints no path. memoro's `scripts/shot/shot.mjs` does not honour `click` yet (2026-10-18), so until it does every `--click` ends in that refusal.' In the sentence after the list ('The request gains `safe_area`, … after `out`'), add: 'and `click` after `onboarding`'. In `docs/mc-command-matrix.md`, the `mc shot` row (line 71): add `[--click <selector>]…` to the synopsis after `[--locale <code>]`, and to the description: ' `--click` (repeatable) is pressed in order before the picture; a result that does not answer `clicked` exits 1, which is every result until memoro's capture script supports it.' Put both docs edits in a last commit that touches nothing else.

Tests in `tests/mc/commands/flags.test.js`, inside `describe('scanArgs')`: 'a repeatable flag collects every value in order, and is [] when absent': `scanArgs(['dev', '--click', 'a', 'x', '--click', 'text=Tasks'], { repeatable: ['--click'] })` gives `flags.click` deepEqual `['a', 'text=Tasks']` and `positional` `['dev', 'x']`; `scanArgs(['dev'], { repeatable: ['--click'] }).flags.click` deepEquals `[]`; `scanArgs(['--click'], { repeatable: ['--click'] }).error` is `'--click needs a value'`; `scanArgs(['--click', '--json'], { booleans: ['--json'], repeatable: ['--click'] }).error` is `'--click needs a value'`.

Tests in `tests/mc/shot.test.js`. In `FAKE_SCRIPT` (line 25), add to the success result object `...(request.click && how !== 'no-click' ? { clicked: request.click } : {})`. In 'builds the request the contract fixes' (line 195), append `'click'` after `'onboarding'` in the expected keys and assert `request.click === null`. New tests in `describe('mc shot — the run')`: (1) '--click is handed over in order, and the path comes first': `const fx = fixture(); const result = await shot(['dev', 'home', '--click', '[data-tab="tasks"]', '--click', 'text=Tasks'], fx);` gives code 0, `sideOf(fx).request.click` deepEquals `['[data-tab="tasks"]', 'text=Tasks']`, and `result.stdout.split('\n')[0]` equals the request's `out`. (2) 'a script that does not answer clicked is refused, and no path is printed': `shot(['dev', 'home', '--click', 'text=Tasks'], fx, { behaviour: 'no-click' })` gives code 1, `stdout` '' and `stderr` matching `/^mc: the picture at .*\.png was taken without the clicks — this memoro's capture script does not answer clicked, so --click is not supported yet \(memoro's scripts\/shot\/shot\.mjs has to honour request\.click\)\n/mu`. (3) 'without --click the request carries null and nothing is asked of the result': `shot(['dev', 'home'], fx, { behaviour: 'no-click' })` gives code 0 and `request.click` null. Also unit-test `clickGap` in `describe('mc shot — the pieces')`: null for `({ click: null }, {})`, null for `({ click: ['a'] }, { clicked: ['a'] })`, a string for `({ click: ['a', 'b'] }, { clicked: ['a'], file: '/o.png' })` and for `({ click: ['a'] }, { file: '/o.png' })`; import `clickGap` beside `buildRequest`.

Test in `tests/mc/shot-compare.test.js`, in `describe('mc shot dev --compare')`: '--click reaches both sides, and a side that does not answer clicked fails': give `compare()` an option `clicked = { here: true, ref: true }` whose stub `runCapture` adds `clicked: request.click` to a side's result only when `clicked[side]` and `request.click`. `compare(['dev', 'assistant', '--click', 'text=Tasks', '--compare', 'origin/main'])` gives code 0, and both captured requests have `click` deepEqual `['text=Tasks']`. With `{ clicked: { here: true, ref: false } }` it gives code 1 and `stderr` matching `/mc: origin\/main: the picture at .* was taken without the clicks/u`.

Add `changelog.d/shot-click.md` with `section: Added`: '**`mc shot --click <selector>`, repeatable.** A pane behind a tab or a window behind a button could only be pictured by declaring a target in memoro's `.mc/shot.json`, so on 2026-10-17 a session wrote its own Playwright script instead. The clicks go to the capture script as the request's `click`, in order, and a result that does not answer `clicked` exits 1 with no path, since its picture lacks them. memoro's capture script does not honour `click` yet, so until it does that refusal is what `--click` answers.'

`mc gate tests/mc/commands/flags.test.js tests/mc/shot.test.js tests/mc/shot-compare.test.js`, then `mc gate`, `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`. This is the plan's last step: in the same PR set every `success_criteria[].met` in this plan to true.
